title: spec_parse
description: What a model may read out of a plain-language lead request. Deliberately narrower than ResearchSpec: everything here is something the user actually said. Defaults, limits and credit policy are added deterministically afterwards (app/ai/spec_draft.py), so the model never invents them.

intent.description: Why the user wants these leads.

seed_company.description: The business the request is about: the one to profile, or the one to find competitors of. Null when the request names no particular company.

industry_terms.description: The business types asked for, in the user's own words, lowercased and singular where natural ('restaurant', 'dental clinic'). Empty when no business type was named.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2, uppercase. Null unless the country is named or unmistakable from the places named.

states.description: State or region names exactly as the user wrote them.

cities.description: City, town or locality names exactly as the user wrote them.

radius_km.description: Only when the user gave a distance, e.g. 'within 10 km of Andheri'.

has_website.description: True when the user asked only for businesses with a website, false when only for ones without, null when they did not say.

fields.description: Columns the user asked for. Only what they named; the planner adds the defaults for the intent.

depth.description: How hard to look. Null unless the user signalled it ('just a quick list', 'go deep').

max_results.description: Only when the user gave a number, e.g. 'top 50 cafes'.

exclude_existing.description: True when the user asked to skip leads they already have.

unsupported.description: Constraints the user stated that no field here can carry, in their own words (a star rating, a technology, a hiring signal). The user is told these are not applied rather than being charged for results that ignore them.

ambiguities.description: Short questions to put to the user where the request is genuinely unclear. Empty when it is clear enough to run.

confidence.description: How well this reading matches the request, 0 to 1. Be honest: a vague request deserves a low number and the user will be asked instead of being charged.
